details:
This is a feature that will inevitably draw bad optics but is still going to be a responsible thing to establish on this platform.
Having attended many rave/dance events in VRC now, it has become clear to me that VRChat needs some way for players to define emergency contacts that can be accessed by their friends in-game in the event of an emergency. Seeing players pass out isn't exactly uncommon - and unfortunately on their backs as well - and typically their friends have no real way to contact them or alert medical services when these issues occur.
This could work in any number of ways - allowing players to pick and choose who they want to share this contact information with, or by creating some kind of system where a friend that notices you're having issues can send a ping to your client and if no response is received within a certain period of time - and you're not afk, emergency contact information is displayed.
"But you can already do this through other platforms with those you trust..."
Yes, but having this information available readily within the client itself is valuable in that it saves response time and streamlines the process of reporting when your friend is in medical need. Also, having it within the client will go a long way toward getting the conversation rolling on this before it becomes more of a widespread issue.
"Won't this look bad for VRC? Media outlets will run wild about people passing out / dying in VRC."
Yes, but as these events continue to grow in popularity this will eventually happen anyway. Someone is going to die at LONER, Shelter, etc. if this hasn't happened already. It's just a matter of time. Ultimately, these kinds of situations are par for the course at raves/concerts but typically it's possible to actually help someone in meatspace - even if they have no relation to you whatsoever. In VRC there is no way to do so in most cases. Still, having the ability to list emergency contact information and display it on an opt-in basis (with maybe some level of escrow) to those you trust would go a long way to simply raising awareness and could hopefully save a few lives in the worst circumstances.
Many will of course choose to not use these features - for obvious reasons. Still, I think VRC has some responsibility - as a social platform - to at least provide them to players who would use them.
title: Emergency contacts
